fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah, all people of Judah and Jerusalem who enter through these gates." (Jeremiah 17:20) Kings and the people of Judah and Jerusalem get the very same message. Nobody gets a side door.

Elders and judges are not named here, friend. The LORD calls out "…O kings of Judah, all people of Judah and Jerusalem who enter through these gates." (Jeremiah 17:20) So the message goes to the kings and the people of Judah and Jerusalem. Nobody in that crowd gets to say the memo wasn't for them.

Priests and prophets don't show up in this call, baker. The LORD says, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah, all people of Judah and Jerusalem who enter through these gates." (Jeremiah 17:20) That's the kings plus the people of Judah and Jerusalem. It's a message for the whole bunch the LORD names.

That's right, baker. The LORD says, "Go and stand at the gate of the people, through which the kings of Judah go in and out; and stand at all the other gates of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 17:19) So it's the gate of the people AND all the others. That's a whole lot of gates for one prophet.

Right on, friend. The LORD says, "…but you must keep the Sabbath day holy, just as I commanded your forefathers." (Jeremiah 17:22) No loads and no work, and the day is kept holy. That's the command, plain and simple.
Close in sound, baker, but not the word. The LORD says, "…this city will be inhabited forever." (Jeremiah 17:25) Not once more. Forever, and that's a lot longer than once more.

That's it, friend. The LORD says people will come "…bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and frankincense, and thank offerings to the house of the LORD." (Jeremiah 17:26) That's if the people listen. They come from the cities of Judah and the places around Jerusalem with their gifts.

Benjamin shows up in the promise, friend. If the people listen, others will come from "…the land of Benjamin…" bringing offerings. (Jeremiah 17:26) But the fire in verse 27 is for if they don't listen, and it consumes "…the citadels of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 17:27) It's a heavy part of the passage.

The Negev shows up in the promise, baker. If the people listen, others will come from "…the hill country, and the Negev…" bringing offerings. (Jeremiah 17:26) The fire is for if they don't listen, and it is set to "…consume the citadels of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 17:27) It's a heavy warning, so let's take it seriously.
